decisions.decision: A conflict pauses only work that depends on the conflicting authority, fact, artifact, resource, or unsafe shared store. Independent authorized work continues.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: Conflict Scope; Should only block dependent work
decisions.limits: Preserve genuine user/host-wide stops. A prepared multi-file native transaction can make all operations using that canonical store dependent on recovery; do not remove Pending() integrity barriers.

decisions.decision: Corrected debug and reviewer submissions may be resubmitted. Preserve rejected history and use fresh linked attempts where the existing request is terminal.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: Debug and reviewer policy yes they can be resubmitted
decisions.limits: Input correction is not an authority grant. Actual host/user denial, changed subject scope, missing trust and unsafe cleanup remain controlling. Exact retry of the same operation replays its recorded result; a changed attempt is a new identity.

decisions.decision: Include the actual canonical SMARTS lenses and material alternatives for B and the receiving CLI agent to decide progress versus evidence semantics.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: progress versus evidence - Add SMARTS lenses to the CLI packet for me to go over with the receiving agent
decisions.limits: The preferred option in the worksheet is a recommendation, not user approval. Native output closure, discovery, binding limits and retirement fixes can proceed independently.

decisions.decision: Implement functional Pi child authors through an actual supported scoped parent delegation contract.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: pi child authors - implement actual supported scoped parent delegation
decisions.limits: Parent authorization, plan mode, trust, lifecycle and bridge hard blocks remain controlling. Read-only/unavailable is a valid temporary degraded state, not completion. Action scope does not imply OS filesystem/network containment for arbitrary commands.

decisions.decision: Add durable interruption recovery while keeping ordinary work nonblocking wherever safe.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: new durable interruption recovery - add it and keep ordinary work nonblocking as possible
decisions.limits: Recovery records do not grant remote publication, expanded cleanup or new authority. Optional harvest failure is visible and recoverable without a universal progress gate; uncertain external effects require observation before retry.

decisions.decision: Include concrete ADR successor/addendum suggestions in the handoff and reconcile them with implementation.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: governance changes put ADR update suggestions in the hand off
decisions.limits: User approved preparing the suggestions. Existing accepted historical bodies and authority records remain immutable except the sanctioned supersession/status mechanism. The proposed texts are not already accepted ADRs.

decisions.decision: Keep the complete program on a separate integration branch until it is entirely implemented and tested; then promote it for a new major product release.
decisions.source: User response, 2026-11-09: move this work into a seperate branch where it will remain until it is is entirely finished and tested at which point we will drop a new major version release
decisions.limits: No partial program merges into main. Child branches integrate into major/state-contracts. Main-only publisher/deployer guards stay active. Final release needs the exact accepted source and tested artifacts.

decisions.decision: Resolve HIGH severity versus reviewer gate disposition with B/maintainer; resubmission permission alone does not settle this rule.
decisions.source: Audit W-F03 plus limited scope of the explicit resubmission answer
decisions.limits: Do not silently make every HIGH advisory or every maintenance HIGH blocking. Keep independent work moving while the specific contract is discussed.
